### Locomotion blend space (M40-T4; client only, not simulated)

From the M40 audit (defect D4): a moving marine showed one discrete clip, the nearest of eight directions in one speed band (M36, M27), so
between two directions' headings the feet slid by up to half the speed (planted-foot speed median 1.2 to 1.4 m/s at the headings between the clip
directions, steps of 30 to 45 cm), and the clip flickered when the heading reversed. Now the relaxed run, the ready (hip-fire) run and the sprint
are a **blend** of the neighbouring clips with weights from the ground velocity, phase-synced by the feet, with the legs corrected where the
blend bends them. **The sprint is not blended by default** (review S1): on the first sweep demos its standing foot slid more than the old three-way blend, so it keeps the
M36 blend; `--gait-sprint` turns the gait blend on for it (a **regression** there until it measures no worse). Same for the own marine and remote ones (it needs only the state's velocity, facing and pitch). Nothing here changes the
simulation or the protocol. Code: `SmContent/ClipGait.cs`, `GaitBlend.cs`, `GaitLibrary.cs` (engine-free; tests `tests/SmNet.Tests/GaitBlendTests.cs`,
synthetic numbers only), `client/NetworkView.GaitBlend.cs`, `CharacterViewer.cs` (`BlendStance`), `CharacterViewer.LegIk.cs`, `NetworkView.Locomotion.cs`,
`NetworkView.HipFire.cs`. `--no-gait-blend` (test aid) restores the M36 / M27 nearest-clip poses, `--no-leg-ik` the plain rotation blend, `--gait-sprint` blends the sprint too, `--log-footsteps` prints the footstep tags that fire. The M36 rows
"which clip shows (relaxed)", "which clip shows (sprint)" for the clip choice and "playback rate" are replaced by the rows below whenever the gait data is
loaded (they remain the fallback). The graphs blend these clips continuously too (`FLT_Nav_Motion_Angle_DAMPED`, `FLT_Input_Nav_Speed_DAMPED`,
`FLT_Nav_Motion_Angle_SPRINT_DAMP`); what the original's blend does with its sync events and variables is not decoded, so everything below that is not a
clip's measured number is **interpretation**.

| Parameter (M40-T4) | Value | Units | Timing basis | Where | Source | Kind | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Foot-plant sync events | `SYNC_L1`, `SYNC_R1` are in the event list of `SM_Bolter_NAV` but **no sequencer carries them as a tag** (`smtool graph-dump SM_Bolter_NAV`: the walk / run sequencer `SequencerGenerator00` has no tags), and the run, walk and sprint clips have **no annotation tracks** (`hkaAnimation` annotation array @28 read: 0 tracks on `SM_NAV_Run_F_01`, `Walk_F_01`, `Run_R_01`, `Run_B_01`, `SM_MP_1HR_NAV_Sprint_F`). The sync points are therefore derived from the motion: the circular mean of the planted times of each foot | - | - | `ClipGait.FromFeet` | graphs, clips | derived (ours) | medium |
| Planted foot (flat) | the toe bone `RIG_L_Toe` / `RIG_R_Toe` within 0.015 m of its lowest point in the clip's cycle and the ankle `RIG_L_Foot` / `RIG_R_Foot` within 0.04 m of its lowest (heel down); the clip sampled 64 times over its length, forward kinematics from the skeleton's reference pose | m | per clip | `ClipGait.ToeBand`, `AnkleBand` | measured from the clips | derived (ours) | medium |
| Stride (m of body travel per cycle) | minus the planted foot's horizontal velocity times the clip length; the velocity is 0.4 x the mean + 0.6 x the median of the planted samples (the median is the speed of the flat part, what a viewer sees slide; the mean returns the foot to where it landed; the toe rolls on and off at other speeds, up to 1 m/s on the back run); the mean's share shrinks in proportion when less than 0.3 of the cycle is planted (the sprint's is 0.1: its heel-lift samples would skew it). 0.4 chosen on the sweep demos: 0.0 left steps of 18 cm on the back headings of the rifle demo, 0.3 steps of 15.5 to 15.9 cm on two demos, 0.4 steps of 12 to 15 cm with the flat foot sliding at 0.28 to 0.30 m/s | m | per clip | `ClipGait.MeanShare`, `FullShareFraction` | measured, mix ours | derived (ours) | medium |
| Measured clip gaits (rifle relaxed run, `GaitLibrary`) | run F 0.867 s, stride 5.60 m (6.47 m/s), FR / FL 5.6 m (6.5 m/s), R / L 5.13 m (5.92 m/s), BR / BL 4.2 m (4.8 m/s), B 4.03 m (4.64 m/s); walk F / B / R 2.6 m per 1.333 s (1.94 m/s); sprint F 5.12 m per 0.633 s (8.08 m/s; the simulation's sprint is 10 m/s, so it plays 1.24x), strafes 5.5 / 5.1 m at -45 / +45 degrees. The simulation's speeds are run 6.5, strafe 6, back 4.5: the clips match within 5 % except the sprint. Left and right strafes now agree (the M36 table has R 5.55, L 5.65, B 4.5: its toe-band measure was noisy). All 81 clips of the relaxed run (rifle, pistol), sprint (3 families) and ready run (3 families, level-aim clips) are read at load on a worker thread; sync R - L is 0.48 to 0.54 of the cycle in all | m, m/s | per clip | the gait table | measured | measured | high |
| Phase | 0 at the left foot's plant, 0.5 at the right foot's, 1 at the next left plant; a clip's time maps to it piecewise linearly between its two sync points (half the clip each when the sync data is implausible); blended clips play at the same phase, so they have the same foot on the ground whatever their length or where the stride starts in the file | - | per frame | `GaitPhase` | derived | derived (ours) | medium |
| Blend space | directions placed by their **stride's** angle (not the label: a clip named 45 that travels 40 is placed at 40): eight round the body for the relaxed and ready runs (cyclic), three at -45 / 0 / +45 for the sprint (the ends clamp). Bands: walk and run per direction (the sprint has one). Weights: the two neighbouring directions x the two neighbouring bands; the band share from the speed (the walk and run strides blend linearly with it), the direction share from requiring the blended stride to point along the velocity (one cross product); cadence = \|velocity\| / \|blended stride\| cycles per second, clamped to 0.6 to 1.5 x the blend's natural cadence (the weights' mean of 1 / clip length; the old playback clamps were 0.6 to 1.5 walk, 0.7 to 1.4 run). The clamp is the only place the planted feet cancel the velocity inexactly | - | per frame | `GaitSpace.Solve` | derived | derived (ours) | medium |
| Ready run | the same blend over the ready posture's directions and walk / run bands (`HipFireAnimations`); each (direction, band) is a down / level / up triple weighted by the aim pitch as before (M27); the standing aim triple (`SM_NAV_IdleLFocus_S_Aim*`, the pistol and heavy equivalents) is the idle share. Aim mode (Left Ctrl) keeps its nearest-clip poses (M20) | - | per frame | `NetworkView.HipGaitFamily` | as above | derived (ours) | medium |
| Idle share | the moving clips' weight rises linearly from 0 at standstill to 1 at 1.0 m/s, the idle pose takes the rest, so a reversal through zero speed passes through the idle pose instead of flipping from one direction's clip to the other's (the original's walk-on-the-spot clip sits at the speed-0 end of the same blend; the ready run and the sprint use the idle pose, as M36; **the relaxed run uses the walk-on-the-spot clip since animation pass 1**: the idle share then ends at 0.35 m/s, see "Fall pose, hard landing, walk-on-the-spot and the layer stack"). A marine enters the movement poses above 0.5 m/s (`RunThreshold`) and leaves them when its damped speed is below 0.2 m/s | m/s | per frame | `GaitBlend.MovingWeight`, `IdleBlendSpeed`, `GaitLeaveSpeed` | choice: ours | interpretation | low |
| Damping | the ground velocity the weights follow is the simulation's, low-pass filtered with an exponential time constant of 0.06 s (about two ticks; the simulation reaches full speed in 0.125 s), rotated into the body's current facing; it snaps after a gap of more than 0.25 s without drawing or a jump of more than 30 m/s | s | per frame | `VelocityDamper` | choice: ours | interpretation | low |
| Dominant clip | a blend layer reports its largest-weight clip (clips with a gait win ties) as the clip `ClipTime` / `Playing` give (the sound tags, the probes), held until another leads by 0.2 of the total weight (about the old 8 degree direction hold) | - | per frame | `CharacterViewer.DominantHysteresis` | choice: ours | interpretation | low |
| Leg correction | blended local rotations bend the legs to a pose neither clip has (measured: the blended toe sank up to 8 cm below the ground on the back diagonals and the planted foot drifted). Positions blend linearly, so after the pose is built each leg is solved by two-bone IK (thigh, calf; the foot keeps its blended orientation; the knee keeps its blended bend) to the weighted mean of the blended clips' ankles in model space (forward kinematics of each clip's sampled pose). The share is the blend layers' fade, so cross-fades from other stances ease in. While one clip plays the correction is 0.2 cm on average. Not the ground-adaptive foot IK of the audit's T11 | m | per frame | `CharacterViewer.LegIk.cs` | choice: ours | interpretation | medium |
| Rotation sign reference | every clip's rotation is flipped to the hemisphere of the pose shown last, not of whichever clip is added first (`q` and `-q` are one rotation), so a blend cannot jump when its first clip drops out | - | per frame | `CharacterViewer._signRef` | choice: ours | interpretation | high |
| Footsteps | the `EVT_Left_Foot` / `EVT_Right_Foot` tags (behaviour Action tags of the run clips, at about phase 0.9 and 0.4 of the gait cycle) of a marine in a blend layer fire on the crossing of the shared gait phase, not on the reported clip's own time (a change of the reported clip reset the clip-time logic and could double-fire or drop a step): the tags of every clip with weight >= 0.2 are placed on the phase through their clip's sync points and never fire twice within 0.35 cycles. Headless 75 s replay with `--log-footsteps` (sound loaded): footsteps per player 125 and 128 against 129 and 127 the phase counts (2 per cycle), the clip-time logic of `--no-gait-blend` 137 and 133; 6 and 3 repeats of the same foot against 0 and 3 (a repeat is a step dropped while the blend left and re-entered at a stop) | cycles | per frame | `NetworkView.SoundBlendTags` | choice: ours | interpretation | medium |
| Failure isolation, load cost | the gait data is optional: `GaitLibrary.Load` runs the gait analysis (and the hip-fire read it needs) under a broad catch (not out-of-memory) and returns an empty library with a note, and one clip that fails costs only that clip, so the sprint and relaxed-run data and the nearest-clip poses survive (tests). The worker's decoded clips are handed to the rig's cache (`RigAssets.Preload`), so the first moving frame does not decode them again on the main thread; the clip samples of a frame use one buffer (`HavokSplineAnimation.SampleInto`) | - | at load, per frame | `GaitLibrary.Guard`, `Build` | choice: ours | - | high |

Run on a `--record-demo` recording: `--play-demo <file> --headless --fixed-fps 60 --anim-probe --pose-pop-probe` | m/s, cm, degrees | per frame | `client/AnimProbe.cs` | test aid | - | - |

**Result.** The same recorded demo replayed headless at 60 fps on one build with `--no-gait-blend` (before) and without (after). The three demos are
`--bot-gait --gait-sweep` bots (two clients, one recorded): 142 s, 75 s with shots every 3 s (ready run), 75 s. Walk and run bands, flat foot, worst of the
sixteen 22.5 degree headings. Audit T4 acceptance: planted-foot speed median < 0.3 m/s and < 15 cm per step at every heading; <= 1 stance change per
0.3 s while strafing. Kind `measured` (our probes), confidence medium (one build).

| Demo | Planted-foot speed median, worst heading (m/s) | Step slide median, worst heading (cm) | All steady frames: speed median / step median (m/s, cm) | Clip changes during steady strafing |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 142 s relaxed run, before | 1.24 | 37.3 | 0.68 / 14.2 | 16 in 53 s |
| 142 s, after | **0.28** | **11.8** | 0.21 / 4.3 | 3 in 53 s |
| 75 s ready run, before | 1.14 | 40.0 | 0.67 / 15.8 | 8 in 26 s |
| 75 s ready run, after | **0.29** | **14.9** | 0.20 / 4.1 | 2 in 26 s |
| 75 s relaxed run, before | 1.36 | 35.8 | 0.67 / 14.0 | 7 in 26 s |
| 75 s, after | 0.30 (22.5 degrees, 63 frames; the others 0.17 to 0.29) | **12.8** | 0.23 / 4.6 | 1 in 26 s |

The other weapon families (75 s demos, shots every 3 s): **heavy bolter** (`--class devastator`, always ready; its ready run has four directions 90 degrees apart) before 3.20 m/s and 71 cm at the worst heading, after 0.40 m/s and 19.5 cm (worst at the back and the back diagonals; all steady frames 1.13 to 0.26 m/s, steps 32.4 to 3.9 cm); **pistol** (`--class tactical --bot-slot pistol`) before 1.16 m/s and 34.1 cm, after 1.07 m/s (135 degrees only: the pistol's back-right run clip has stretches where the foot stands still against the body while the body moves, so no single stride fits it; every other heading 0.17 to 0.40) and 16.0 cm (180 degrees; all steady frames 0.71 to 0.29 m/s, steps 20.9 to 5.4 cm). Not met for those two families.

**Cost** (sixteen headless sweep bots on one machine against one server, 60 s, the measured client logs `--anim-probe --frame-stats`; every client runs the same code, so the machine is saturated and the frame times are noisy): the characters' pose work per rendered frame (stances, clip samples, leg correction; 16 marines drawn) median 0.52 ms, mean 0.67, p99 2.77, worst 97.0 before (`--no-gait-blend`) and median 1.30, mean 1.53, p99 6.82, worst 96.2 after (about 0.07 ms more per moving marine and frame); frame time median 6.90 / 6.94 ms, p99 36.1 / 32.2, p99.9 121 / 76, worst 140 / 122 before / after, i.e. no difference the noise does not hide. The 97 ms worst pose frame is in both runs (a first-use hitch outside this work). Samples of a frame use one buffer (no allocation per clip); the clips the worker decoded are handed to the rig cache instead of decoded again on the main thread.

Without the leg correction (`--no-leg-ik`, 142 s demo) the worst heading is 1.05 m/s and 56 cm, the toe sinks to -8 cm (after: -1.8 cm; before: -16 cm, from the old
stance cross-fades). With the toe alone as the planted test (stricter on the toe roll: it counts the toe-pivot at the end of a stance) the worst heading is 0.29 to
0.33 m/s and 17.5 to 25.3 cm. The noise of the measure is about 0.03 m/s and 1 to 2 cm (re-tuning the stride estimate moved the demos by that much). The measure's
floor is about 0.2 m/s: the toe rolls and the drawn body moves in 60 Hz steps.

Not met or not better: the **sprint** with `--gait-sprint` (planted-foot speed of the standing part of the stance 0.37 m/s against 0.17 to 0.28 before; the sprint's flat foot lasts 4 to 6
frames, and the swing foot grazes the ground at up to 20 m/s for 1 to 2 frames of every step in both versions, which the height test counts as planted, so its step slides
are 30 to 34 cm in both) is therefore off by default: the shipped sprint is the M36 blend, 0.21 m/s against 0.20 on the 142 s demo; the **dominant clip** changes more often (flip-flops 52 against 14 in the 142 s demo, 31 against 1 to 4 in the shorter ones: at a reversal the
walk and run weights of the same direction cross as the speed passes through zero; the pose between them is continuous, the stances were not); the largest
one-frame bone turns are the clips' authored loop seams on the prop bones `RIG_Prop_M_Rhand` / `RIG_Prop_LHand` (112 / 113 degrees once per cycle before and after; the
weapon mount bones are `RIG_Prop_M_Chest` and `RIG_Prop_LHand`: the left-hand seam that fired 52 times before fires 0 times now). Knee angles while moving are unchanged
(median 118 against 120 degrees, 1st percentile 52 against 49, 99th 152 against 157). Aim-walk (Left Ctrl) is still the nearest of its eight clips.

### Action clips hand the legs to the locomotion (M40-T4 follow-up; client only, not simulated)

From the owner's live playtest: after an F stun strike, when the player moved again as soon as allowed, the character slid along the ground. The simulation lets the
player move while some actions are still playing; the clips are whole-body and stand in place. Sweep of every action (a bot doing each in turn with the stick held
forward, `--action-sweep`, then `--anim-probe`'s action table on a recorded demo, before = `--no-handoff`): the melee attacks from their `MoveAt` and the grenade
throw were the only ones that kept the whole body under a moving marine. Code: `client/NetworkView.Handoff.cs`, a few lines in `NetworkView.cs` `Place`
(the attack and the throw call `HandoffAttack` / `HandoffThrow` before posing the clip), `NetworkView.HipFire.cs` (the cross-fade override), the probe in `AnimProbe.cs`.

| Parameter (M40-T4 follow-up) | Value | Units | Timing basis | Where | Source | Kind | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hand-off of a melee attack | from the step's `MoveAt` (`BRANCH_Melee_Draw_Run` / `BRANCH_Melee_Run`, the simulation's own movement-lock end, `MeleeStep.MoveAt`) while the body moves on the ground (> 0.5 m/s; once handed over it stays until the step ends or a new one starts): the legs and everything else follow the locomotion blend, cross-faded over 0.1 s ("Default 3 Frame Transition", `ClipBlends.Default`), and the attack clip stays on the **upper body** (the reload's bone mask, `HipFireSet.UpperBodyMask`: legs 0, the rest 1) until its end, its weight falling to 0 over the last 0.15 s (the `MoveAt` test and the tail use the posed time, the smoothed clock for remote players; the mask's prop bones and arms have weight 1, so the weapon follows: `smtool graph-dump --reload`). Without the mask (the hip-fire data not loaded yet, `--no-hip-fire`, a family without a reload blend) nothing is handed over and the whole-body clip shows as before; the body must be alive, grounded and not in a jump-pack phase. The clip's tag sounds keep firing from its own time (`SoundLayerTags`). Rules: `SmNet.ActionHandoff` (tested). Covers light steps, combo ends, heavy and stun strikes | s, m/s | per frame | `NetworkView.HandoffAttack` | data (`MoveAt`), the rest ours | data (when), interpretation (how) | medium |
| Hand-off of a grenade throw | the throw never locks movement: from the first moving frame (> 0.5 m/s, grounded) the toss clip is an upper-body layer over the locomotion (weight in over 0.1 s when the throw starts moving, out over the last 0.15 s of `ThrowDuration`) | s | per frame | `NetworkView.HandoffThrow` | choice: ours | interpretation | medium |
| Clips that already end with the simulation's state | reactions (interrupt, stagger, stun, blast, knockback, get-up): the state ends at `BRANCH_Run` when the stick is held, until then the body is pushed only; the charge and its collision stop: at `BRANCH_Attack2Idle` (`RushMove.MoveAt`) when the stick, Fire, Aim or a grenade ask; rolls and hops: at `BRANCH_Run` (`EvadeMove.MoveAt`); the jump landings and the pound's get-up: at their move lock (`NetworkView.Jump.cs`); reload: a masked layer over the legs (M35); weapon switch: no body clip; respawn: a new life starts in the locomotion. Not changed | - | - | `ReactionClip`, `RushMove`, `EvadeMove` | graphs | data | high (by reading); reactions and the charge not exercised by the bot |

The probe's table: per action clip that still shows (a clip drives the pose, or lies over the locomotion as the upper-body layer) while the body moves (>= 1.5 m/s over 0.1 s): clip frames, seconds moving, longest run, planted-foot (flat) slide median and p90 | m/s, s | per frame | `NetworkView.ActionSweep.cs`, `AnimProbe.cs` | test aid | - | - |

### Turn in place, aim-offset idle, stop foot pins and run start (M40-T5; client only, not simulated)

From the M40 audit (defects D8 and D9): a standing marine's body took the view's yaw at once (180 degrees in one frame on a flick), its idle was one clip that ignored the aim, a
stop was the run cycle cross-fading into the idle (the planted foot slid 22 to 37 cm) and a start the idle cross-fading into the walk and run blend. Now (the same for the own marine
and remote ones; the simulation, the hit volumes, the shots and the camera keep the view's yaw; **owner's decision still pending: the shown body may lag the aim**) the graphs' own
turn, aim-offset and start states are read (`smtool graph-dump --turns`, `SmContent.TurnAnimations`; engine-free rules `SmNet.BodyYaw`, `SmNet.AimOffsetGrid`, `SmContent.StartMatch`;
tests `TurnInPlaceTests`, `TurnAnimationsTests`) and the client drives them (`NetworkView.TurnInPlace.cs`, `NetworkView.RunStart.cs`, `CharacterViewer.Turn.cs`,
`CharacterViewer.FootPin.cs`). Test aids: `--no-turns` (the old rigid body and single idle; also turns off the pins and the start), `--no-foot-pins`, `--no-run-start`,
`--bot-turn-sweep` (with `--bot --bot-gait`; `--turn-sweep-fire` keeps the weapon up), `--anim-probe` (adds `TurnProbe`: body yaw per frame, planted-foot slide after stops and starts,
barrel against the aim; `--turn-probe-events`, `--turn-probe-trace <s>`), `--run-start-log`.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

The weights are the two neighbouring columns by the angle and in each the two neighbouring clips by the pitch, linear (`AimOffsetGrid`; Havok's blender normalises the same two children). The pistol ("Twist Idle") and the heavy bolter ("Heavy Idle") have only the pitch clips (`SM_1HR_NAV_IdleL_S_*`, `SM_NAV_TB_Idle_S_*`) and a twist modifier bound to the clamped horizontal angle: done here as a rotation of `RIG_SpineA` (40 %) and `RIG_SpineD` (60 %) about the vertical axis, up to 90 degrees. Measured barrel against the aim while standing (rifle, headless bot, 0 to 90 degrees off the body): median 1.1 to 2.5 degrees (the old ready idle 0.5; the old relaxed idle 48: `SM_NAV_IdleL_S_01` carries the rifle low) | degrees | per frame | `TurnStandPlace`, `AimOffsetGrid` | graphs (clips, angles, pitch keys); the linear weights, the twist split and its limit: ours | data (clips, keys), interpretation (weights, twist) | medium |
| Turn threshold | The graph turns when the aim is more than 90 degrees (rifle) or 75 degrees (pistol, heavy bolter) off the body: the transitions from the idle state to the turn states test `FLT_Aim_Horizontal_Deg(_DAMPED)` in [-180, -90] / [90, 180] (rifle), [-180, -75] / [75, 180] (pistol, heavy). Read from the transition conditions | degrees | per frame | `TurnPosture.EnterDegrees` | graphs | data | high |

The turn child's bone mask: the root, pelvis, thighs, calves, feet, toes and knee pads at 1, everything else 0; the aim-offset idle drives the rest. Blend in and between turns 0.1 s ("Turn To Turn") | degrees, s | per frame | `BodyYaw`, `TurnClip`, `SetTurnLayer` | graphs, clips | data | high |
| Turn speed | The graph binds the clip's playback speed to `FLT_TurnSpeedMultiplier` (not decoded); the clips play at their own speed (162 degrees a second) | - | - | `BodyYaw.Step` | - | ours | low |

Aim mode (Left Ctrl) has no turn: the graph's aim stand turns only for AI (`not BOOL_IsPlayerControlled`) and the heavy bolter's aim goes to its rigid spin, so the body follows the aim there | - | per frame | `NetworkView.TurnStanding` | graphs (the aim stand), the rest ours | data (aim), interpretation | medium |

The upper body's aim-offset reaches 90 degrees; beyond it (mid-turn) the spine twist continues the rest of the angle up to the cap (`FootPinRules.SpineTwist`, review S4; the cap stays 135 degrees: it is the turn clip's own rotation, and a lower cap would drag the body at the follow rate in more flicks), which keeps the barrel near the aim (numbers in the Probes row) | degrees a second, degrees | per frame | `NetworkView.BodyFollowRate`, `BodyMaxTwist` | choice: ours | interpretation | low |

| Stop pins | The cross-fade from the run to the idle slides the planted foot (the run-to-idle blend is 0.333 s relaxed, 0.15 s ready rifle, 0.333 s pistol and heavy bolter, read from the graphs; the blend space's idle share takes over in the last 1 m/s, about 0.03 s after the speed starts to fall faster than 8 m/s squared). From that moment the feet that are on the ground (toe within 4.5 cm of the ground; a foot in the air once its toe is within 2 cm) are pinned at their world position and orientation by two-bone IK (`SolveLeg`) while the pose cross-fades to the idle, for the posture's stop blend + 0.06 s; each then steps (an arc, 7 cm lift, 0.2 s; the second foot 0.16 s later) to where the pose puts it. A pin ends when the marine speeds past 2 m/s or does an action (a client-timed jump view, i.e. landing, ground-pound impact or get-up, counts as one: review S3), when the wanted ankle is more than 3 cm beyond the leg's reach from the hip (aim-walk, a push; review S1), when the drawn body moves more than 1 m in a frame (respawn, round restart, teleport; review S2), and, for the run start's idle hold, whenever the start is reset for any reason (S1). The `SM_NAV_AimTurn_*` clips and their sequencers carry only Branch tags (`BRANCH_Turn_End`, `BRANCH_Turn_To_Turn`), no footstep actions, so a turn makes no footstep sounds (checked in `SM_Bolter_NAV`, `SM_Pistol_NAV`, `SM_TB_NAV`). The original's sprint stop (`SM_NAV_Bullrush2Idle_F_01`, rifle; `SM_1HR_NAV_Sprint_to_Idle`, pistol: 1.33 and 1.53 s, `BRANCH_Sprint_Finished` from 0.625 / 0.54) has 5.8 and 6.2 m of root motion, and the run has no stop clip at all (the blend only), so they are not played: the simulation stops the body in 0.16 s (0.25 s from a sprint), 0.5 to 1.25 m (`SM_NAV_Sprint_to_Idle_F` is the dash attack's, not the sprint's). | Run start | **Off by default since the review (M1): `--run-start` opts in, `--no-run-start` wins; the code is kept.** The numbers below are with it on. The rifle's start clip `SM_TRN_BO_IdleAim_to_RunF` (0.7 s) when the requested speed is 3 or more ("Idle Relaxed To Run Relaxed" / "Idle Ready To Run Ready": `FLT_Input_Nav_Speed_LOGIC` in [3, 10000]; blend in 0.333 s, out 0.1 s relaxed / 0.267 s ready, back to the idle 0.333 / 0.1 s; ends at `BRANCH_Idle_To_Run_End` = the clip's end). ### Fall pose, hard landing, walk-on-the-spot and the layer stack (animation pass 1; client only, not simulated, no protocol change)

From the animation audit of 2026-10-28 (items 1, 5 and 10, and its shared prerequisite) and the owner's description ("in sm1 when a player walks off a ledge he drops as if gravity pulls
him straight down, with a falling animation"). Until now a marine that left the ground kept its run or idle pose for the whole fall and snapped on landing, the zero-speed end of the relaxed
speed blend was the idle pose and the client had one extra pose layer. Now (the same for the own marine and remote ones; the simulation, the hit volumes and the shots are not touched; the
simulation still keeps horizontal speed in a fall, a separate task will change that, and the pose looks right either way because it does not show the horizontal speed in the air):
the fall, its landing and the exits are read from the navigation graphs (`smtool graph-dump --falls`, `SmContent.FallAnimations`, `FallLanding`, `FallRules`; tests
`FallAnimationsTests`, `GaitBlendTests` (walk on the spot)), the client drives them (`NetworkView.Fall.cs`, `NetworkView.GaitBlend.cs`) over a **pose layer stack**
(`CharacterViewer.Layers.cs`). Test aids: `--no-fall-pose`, `--no-wos`, `--no-layer-stack` (every layer back into the one action slot), `--log-fall` (the events and the layers' weights),
`--fall-hard-speed <m/s>` (lowers the rifle's hard-landing speed for tests), `--bot-ledge [--ledge-min-drop m]` (with `--bot --bot-gait`: a bot that plans a straight run off a ledge with the
real movement function, runs it and plans again from where it lands), `--wait-fall` / `--wait-fall-land` (screenshot at 0.35 s into a fall / 0.1 s into the landing clip), `--pose-hash <file>`
(a hash of every drawn character's bones per frame, to compare two builds on one demo replay).

### Weapon switch, hit flinch, death hit and the jump pack's upper body (animation pass 2; client only, not simulated, no protocol change)

From the animation audit of 2026-10-28, using the pass-1 layer stack's free slots. Until now a weapon switch showed no body motion (the model changed in the hand half way through the simulation's
switch time), a non-lethal hit showed nothing on the victim, a kill turned the body into a ragdoll in the pose it died in, the jump pack's flight was a single posed clip and the pound's get-up was the
standing one. Now (the same for the own marine and remote ones; the simulation, hit volumes, shots and the protocol are not touched): the clips are read from the base graph `SM_Base_MP` and the jump pack graph
`MP_SM_NAV_JP_Sim` (`smtool graph-dump --upper`, `SmContent.UpperBodyBundle`: `SwitchAnimations`, `FlinchAnimations`, `DeathAnimations`, `JumpPackAnimations`; engine-free rules `FlinchRules`, `DeathRules`; tests
`UpperBodyAnimationsTests`), the client plays them (`NetworkView.UpperBody.cs`, `NetworkView.Jump.cs`, `WeaponRig.Update`) on three more layer slots (`PoseSlots.Switch` 3, `Flinch` 4, `Wobble` 5; a layer laid
over a clip shown by `Pose()` is now applied again, `CharacterViewer._layersDirty`, and a layer can be a whole-pose clip taken as the offset from its own pose at a reference time). Test aids: `--no-switch-anim`,
`--no-flinch`, `--no-death-anim`, `--no-jump-upper` (each restores the pass-1 behaviour; with all four the pass-1 pose stream is reproduced), `--log-upper` (the events; bots print them anyway).

**The primary is stowed round the right side (fix/stow-right; client only, no protocol change).** The owner's playtest: "tactical marine when stowing their primary weapon to switch to bolt
pistol should stow it to the right around their back not the left. currently the gun floats through the air which looks silly." Cause (measured with `--switch-test --switch-probe
--switch-clips`, positions in `RIG_SpineA`'s frame): every primary (bolter, storm and stalker bolters, plasma gun, melta, grenade launcher, heavy bolter, lascannon, plasma cannon, both races) is
held on `RIG_Prop_M_Chest` and stowed on `MKR_Stow_Bolter` (the small of the back, 5 cm right of the spine); the pistol switch's clip `SM_Swap_Rifle_to_Melee_01` animates that chest prop
round the marine's **left** side (54 cm left of the spine at 0.17 s) onto the marker at its tag (0.4 s), while both hands stay in front: from 0.2 s the prop, and with it the gun, is 0.4 to 0.8 m from
either hand (79 cm at worst while the clip is at full weight). The rifle draw `SM_Swap_Rifle_to_Rifle_01` has the right hand take the chest prop off the marker at its tag (0.233 s: the prop 4 cm
from the marker) and carry it round the **right** side to the front (11 to 14 cm from the right-hand prop from there). Rules and checks: `SwitchPlanTests`; test aids `--switch-test` (with
`--switch-shots`, `--switch-probe`, `--switch-clips`, `--old-stow`), the networked view's `--bot-switch-every s` with `--wait-switch-window a,b`.

### Transitions, connecting clips, the heavy sprint and the pistol idle (animation pass 3; client only, not simulated, no protocol change)

From the owner's playtest of 2026-10-29: "the falling animation is still not blending smoothly with the charge animation, or others for that matter"; "the assault marine and raptor have a weird idle
animation"; "we're missing 'connecting' animations ... it flicks between animation states in a jarring fashion"; "devastator/havoc needs to have a different sprint animation"; "when hopping and
sprinting a devastator/havok needs to keep his weapon in his hands"; "a 'slowdown' when you stop sprinting ... if movement keys are let go of entirely". The reference videos were not watched
(no video access here): the clips, blends and branches below are the install's behaviour graphs (`smtool graph-dump --sprint-edges`, `--pose-diff A B`; `SmContent.SprintTransitions`, tests
`SprintTransitionsTests`); the client plays them (`client/CharacterViewer.Transitions.cs`, `NetworkView.SprintEdges.cs`, `NetworkView.HeavyHold.cs`). Measured with a new probe (`--transition-probe`,
`client/TransitionProbe.cs`) on four recorded sessions (`--bot-gait --transition-sweep`, a bot that goes through the state switches: sprint and let go, run and let go, sprint then run on, roll, charge,
throw, melee, aim, switch, strafe, hop or jump; and `--bot-ledge --ledge-charge`, charges off ledges; Tactical, Devastator, Assault and a Chaos ledge bot, 150 s each) replayed headless at 60 fps,
`--no-p3` for the before. Test aids: `--no-p3` (every change of this section off), `--no-dead-blend`, `--dead-blend-decay <s>`, `--dead-blend-cap <deg/s>`, `--no-sprint-stop`, `--no-sprint-start`,
`--shared-sprint`, `--log-sprint-edges`, `--transition-probe [--transition-probe-csv <file>] [--transition-probe-trace <bone>]`, `--transition-sweep`, `--ledge-charge`.

### Melee flow, the hammer in both hands and the transitions pass (anim/melee-flow; client only, not simulated, no protocol change)

From the owner's requests of 2026-10-29: "Assault Hammer running animation missing"; the power sword and chainsword slash "feels quite janky ... copy the animation from sm1 better"; "add a tiny bit of screen shake to all stun strike moves"; the charge
landing off a ledge; "run a pass where the animations transition much more smoothly ... for all animations". The clips, blends and branches are the install's behaviour graphs (`smtool graph-dump --melee-flow`,
`--locomotion`; `SmContent.MeleeFlowBlends`, `LocomotionAnimations.Hammer`, tests `MeleeFlowTests`); the rules are engine-free (`SmNet.ClipFootLockRules`, `SlashPose`; tests `ClipFootLockRulesTests`); the client is
`client/NetworkView.MeleeFlow.cs` and `client/CharacterViewer.ClipFootLock.cs`. The reference video (`5zCigHGjnI0`, 42.5 to 45.3 s) was looked at frame by frame for the sword's lunges (wide planted stance, the body
carried by the strike); no number was taken from it. Measured with `--anim-probe` and `--transition-probe` (new: `--transition-probe-clips` labels the melee and charge clips by name, so a combo's step to step
counts as a switch) on three recorded sessions replayed headless at 60 fps, `--no-melee-flow` for the before: `melee2` (six melee bots, chainsword, power sword and hammer on both sides, 150 s, bot views turning at
360 degrees a second with the new `--bot-turn-rate`), `sweep` (five `--transition-sweep` bots: Tactical, Devastator, chainsword and hammer Assault, power sword Raptor; the sweep has three new melee legs) and
`ledge` (`--bot-ledge --ledge-charge`). Test aids: `--no-melee-flow` (every change of this section off), `--no-clip-foot-lock`, `--no-stun-shake`, `--stun-shake-scale f`, `--log-stun-shake`, `--charge-turn-snap`,
`--clip-lock-trace <name>`, `--bot-turn-rate <deg/s>`, `--transition-probe-clips`.

Source: behavior graph `MP_SM_MEL_CombatKnife` in `havok_sm_base_mp__hkxx` (sequencers `CK 1/2/3 Sequence`; tag windows
are fractions of the clip, turned into seconds with the playing clip's length divided by its playback speed, 1 for these clips) and wargear `ability_melee_ck1..3`
(default entries). Kind `extracted`; times in seconds from the attack's start; wall clock.

| Attack (clip, 3.5 m variant) | Length | Hit (`ACTN_Hit_Targets_Multiplayer`) | Combo window (`BRANCH_Melee_Combo`) | Fire cancels from (`BRANCH_ToRanged`) | Moves again (`BRANCH_Melee_Draw_Run`) | Damage / secondary | Lunge (`AttackDistance`) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (`SM_MEL_CK_XATK_1_3.5m`) | 1.433 | 0.280 | 0.500–0.769 | 0.433 | 0.779 | 40 / 20 | 3.5 m |
| 2 (`SM_MEL_CK_XATK_2_3.5m`) | 1.500 | 0.384 | 0.533–0.833 | 0.500 | 0.933 | 40 / 20 | 3.5 m |
| 3 (`SM_MEL_CK_XATK_HVY_3.5m_miss`) | 1.933 | 0.533 | 0.604–0.725 | 0.604 | 0.918 | 40 / 20 | 4 m |

The three distance variants of each attack (1 m, 3.5 m, 7 m) have the same length. Attack 3's clips are all "_miss"
variants (no other exists in that sequencer). The upgraded damage (65 primary, 32 secondary) is not used; the stun damage (25)
is inert (`stun_threshold` 1e6; M28). Hit reactions and heavy strikes: section "Hit reactions" (M28).

Notes (from the extraction report; **interpretations** are marked):
- Each `do_damage` also has `damage_armourshield` (extra damage to the regenerating armour shield, **interpretation**),
  per-material multiplier tables (e.g. bolter head ×2.55, heavy armour ×0.5) and piecewise range fall-off.
- Perk files grant only an upgrade name; the weapon file holds alternative entries keyed to it. **Interpretation**: the
  most specific satisfied entry replaces the default (e.g. thunder hammer 200 → 2000 with its AoE perk; knife 40 → 65).
- Spread comes from `climb_sway_scatter` sets per stance (standing / aiming / crouching) and movement (idle / walking /
  running); bolter hip fire: scatter 0.25 initial, +0.35 per shot, max 1.5, recovery 2.4 per second after 0.1 s (applied since
  weapons/spread, the owner's decision of 2026-10-28; see "Weapon spread").
- Only one weapon-driven movement change was found: plasma cannon charging, `speed_maximum` ×0.5.
- Bolter as used (M6, `GameplayTuning.WithWeapon`, default entries): `damage_general` 22; health multipliers
  `damage_material_multipliers/default_body` 1 and `default_head` 2.55; shield multipliers
  `armourshield_damage_material_multipliers/default_body` 0.505 and `default_head` 0.5; `damage_fall_off` points
  (0, ×1), (45, ×1), (70, ×0.8). Hit-zone names (head, body, arms, legs) map hitbox bodies; the shapes are Havok data not
  decoded yet.
- Melee combo windows and hit frames: decoded for the combat knife (table above, M9), the chainsword (M28) and the power sword, power axe, thunder hammer and the heavy classes' kick and stomp (Weapons C, section below).
- Open: how unconditional and per-upgrade damage combine in
  Exterminatus, the meaning of `shot_cooldown` vs `time_between_shots`, and whether `_old` abilities are dead.

### Melee target lock, alignment and lunge (feel/melee-lock; used by the simulation; protocol 32)

From the owner (2026-10-29, the owner's knowledge of SM1): "target locking for melee attacks. when initiating a melee attack or charge or f stun strike,
if the character model is moving in the general direction of an enemy player model they 'stick' to it and line up to keep delivering more melee
attacks. also in general there should be a bit of 'stickiness' to the gameplay ... also, you should step forward when swinging your melee weapon or
combat knife". The data has the parts: the global `directional_targeting_ext` (the targeting cone and reach), each attack sequencer's
`AttackAlignment` window and its clips blended on `FLT_MeleeTargetDistance` at child weights 1, 3.5 and 7 (`…_1m`, `…_3.5m`, `…_7m`) with their
extracted root motion (`smtool graph-dump --melee`). How the engine combined them is not in the data: those rules are ours or interpretations. Code:
`SmSim/MeleeLock.cs` (lock, alignment, lunge; `Combat.StepPlayer` applies them; `World` passes the rewound players), `SmContent/MeleeMotion.cs`
(reach reader), `SmContent/MeleeLockTuning.cs` (global values), `SmNet/GameClient.cs` (`MeleeLockTarget`, `ViewAt`), `SmNet/MeleePresentation.cs`
and `client/NetworkView.MeleeLock.cs` (presentation). Tests: `MeleeLockTests`, `MeleePresentationTests`, `MeleeLockInstallTests` (install only).

| Parameter (feel/melee-lock) | Value | Units | Timing basis | Where | Source | Kind | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lock: who picks it | the client, each tick of a melee press, a heavy press or an attack or charge under way (`MeleeLock.Wants`), with its view tick moved to the nearest snapshot it holds, so its view of the others (`GameClient.ViewAt`) is exactly the server's rewound world at that tick (`World.SeenBy`) and every decision agrees; sent as the input's melee target (u16, 0 none; 38 bytes an input); the server and the client's prediction accept it only while `MeleeLock.Target` does in that tick's phase (stateless: checked every tick, no lock state travels). Other ticks keep their view tick and build no view | — | per tick | `MeleeLock.Choose`, `MeleeLock.Target`, `GameClient.StepTick` | ours (server-authoritative check, client choice) | ours | high |

Measured with headless bots (four Tacticals with the knife, 2 v 2, `--bot-melee --anim-probe`, Manufactorum, 150 s a run on a local server). The bots
aim exactly at their target every tick and stand and tap melee within 3 m, so before protocol 32 their freely turning attack already tracked the target
perfectly; both sides interrupt each other often (a swing the client predicted to its hit but the server interrupted does not land). A swing "landed" when
the server's melee hit report arrives within 0.6 s of its predicted hit. Foot slide: the anim probe's planted-foot speed (flat foot) and planted-stretch
slide under whole-body melee clips, every drawn marine, whatever the body's speed (the four bots' figures).

| Build | Swings | Reached their hit | Landed (of reached / of all swings) | Planted-foot speed median, p90 (m/s) | Planted-stretch slide median (cm) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main 4095ae4 (no lock, no lunge; two runs) | 100 | 86 | 49 (0.57 / 0.49) | 2.88 to 3.21, 7.8 to 8.9 | 60 to 86 |
| this build, `--no-melee-lock` (lunge and held heading, no lock) | 171 | 145 | 74 (0.51 / 0.43) | — | — |
| this build (lock) | 99 | 77 | 59 (0.77 / 0.60) | 2.12 to 2.32, 8.6 to 8.8 | 48 to 52 |
| this build (lock), hit-stop off (`--no-hit-stop`, then the default) | 105 | 90 | 58 (0.64 / 0.55) | 1.87 to 2.03, 8.6 to 9.0 | 50 to 55 |

The lock lands 0.55 to 0.60 of all swings against 0.49 before (run-to-run spread about 0.05) and against 0.43 for the held heading alone; the lunge's foot
slide falls by about a third (median 3.0 to 2.0 m/s, stretch 60 to 86 cm to 48 to 55 cm; the hit-stop adds about 0.2 m/s, by design). The p90 near
8.5 m/s is unchanged in every build: not the lunge (open: the entry cross-fades from a sprint, the remote players' interpolation).

Not done: the `AttackDistanceValidation` window (read, not used), the 180° attacks, player-to-player collision (the lunge stops 1 m short of the locked
target only; it passes through others), the Ork's presentation of its distance clips (its attacks lunge in the simulation; the Ork view still poses its
chosen clip).

### Melee and charge, second pass (feel/melee-charge-2; protocol 42, used by the simulation)

Sources: the owner's requests of 2026-10-29 (verbatim): "landing after ledge charging there is always an additional shoulder bash … when you hit the ground you start doing
the charge animation again. that is wrong. you should in a blended fluid way transition to a running or standing animation if no movement keys are pressed"; "no stomp
available for tacs/assaults by double pressing F. normal combo is backhand > stomp"; "make all melee step forwards step forward more"; weapon switching "is slightly faster
… make a note that this is an estimation and needs to be measured against the original"; the melee and stun lock-ons "feel janky"; and "the power sword currently uses
chainsword sounds". Code: `Rush.EndsOnLanding` / `Landed` / `LandedFrom`, `World.StopRushes` (the landing), `MeleeTuning.CombatKnife` and `MpClasses.ChainSword`
(`YNext`), `SimConfig.MeleeLungeScale` and `MeleeLock.LungeStep` (the lunge), `GameplayTuning.OwnerLungeScale` / `OwnerSwitchScale`, `MeleeLockSpec.AlignEase` /
`MinAlignSpan` / `Hysteresis`, `MeleeLock.Align` / `AlignWindow` / `LockMemory`, `GameClient.RecentMeleeLock`, `MeleePresentation.Assist` / `AssistWeight`,
`SoundTriggers.MeleeHitSound` and `NetworkView.Sound.cs` (`SoundHits`). Tests: `MeleeCharge2Tests` (with the install's numbers, printed), `JumpPackAttackTests` (the
landing), `MeleeLockTests`, `MeleePresentationTests`, `MeleeInstallPinTests`.

### Dedicated server hardening (server/hardening; server only, no protocol change)

For a public tester demo of the dedicated server. The original was peer-hosted, so none of this has an original counterpart: every
value is ours, chosen for abuse resistance, and configurable (`server.cmd --help`; operator notes in docs/dedicated-server.md).
The per-address rules apply only where the transport knows the sender's address (UDP; in-process loopback endpoints without an
address are exempt). Protocol 23 unchanged: refusals reuse `Reject` (`ServerFull` with a detail text), deferrals send nothing.

| Parameter | Value | Units | Timing basis | Where | Source | Kind | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Loopback exemption | loopback addresses (127.0.0.0/8, ::1) are exempt from the per-address cap, the join rate, the per-address respawn hold and the idle kick, so the owner's playtests can run up to 12 bot clients on one machine; `--limit-loopback` applies them to loopback too (tests); bans and the re-join rule on a dead player's own connection apply either way | - | per join | `ServerOptions.LimitLoopback`, `--limit-loopback` | ours (maintainer's request, 2026-10-28) | ours | none |
| Players per address | at most 4 players from one IP address (IPv4-mapped IPv6 counts as IPv4); more are refused with `ServerFull` "at most 4 players from one address"; 0 = no cap | players | per join | `ServerOptions.MaxPlayersPerAddress`, `--max-per-ip` | ours (one household or LAN party behind one NAT) | ours | none |
| Join rate per address | at most one accepted new join per IP address every 5 s; a Hello inside the window gets no answer, so the client's own resend (every 250 ms) gets in once the window has passed; a new client replacing a player on the same address counts as a join; 0 = no limit | s | wall clock (server) | `ServerOptions.JoinInterval`, `--join-interval` | ours | ours | none |
| Idle kick | a player with no real input (any movement or any button; turning alone does not count) and no customizer use (a Setup from the class creator or appearance editor, an emblem upload chunk; appearance queries and blob requests are automatic and do not count) for 300 s while the match is being played is dropped, with no reason shown (the protocol has no kick message: the client shows a lost connection after its server timeout); warm-up and the end of a round reset the clock; only connections with an address are watched (in-process endpoints without one are not); 0 = never | s | wall clock (server) | `ServerOptions.IdleKick`, `--idle-kick`, `GameServer.IsRealInput` | ours | ours | none |
| Repeated Hello of a joined client | answered with the same Welcome but no longer counts as being heard from: a client that only resends its Hello times out after the 5 s peer timeout | - | per packet | `GameServer.OnHello` | ours (before: it refreshed the timeout, so Hellos alone could hold a slot) | ours | none |
| Re-join while dead | a new client on the connection of a dead player, or from the address of a dead player that left, gets no answer until that player's respawn time has run out (5 s placeholder respawn), so a re-join is never a faster respawn or loadout swap; a re-join while alive is a fresh spawn and the death is not scored (open: the original's rule for leavers is unknown) | s | wall clock (server) | `GameServer.AdmitJoin`, `NoteLeave` | ours | ours | none |
| Tick catch-up | at most 5 ticks per server update; after a longer stall the due ticks are skipped (tick phase kept), snapshot and scoreboard times move up to now, and the skip is logged (throttled to one line per 10 s) | ticks | per update | `ServerOptions.MaxCatchUpTicks` | ours (before: unbounded, so a long stall ran every missed tick at once) | ours | none |
| Crash isolation | a packet handler that throws is logged and drops only that sender's player; a recipient whose snapshot fails is dropped alone (the others still get theirs, and the tick's shot records are always cleared); a tick, scoreboard or pickup step that throws is logged and the server goes on; the first 20 faults are logged (the first 5 with stack traces), then one line per 10 s with a count | - | per packet / per tick | `GameServer.Update`, `Dispatch`, `Guard`, `SendSnapshots` | ours | ours | none |
| Failing simulation | after 60 ticks in a row have failed (2 s at 30 Hz) the server logs `FATAL` and exits with code 4 so a supervisor restarts it; a single good tick resets the count; 0 = never | ticks | per tick | `ServerOptions.MaxConsecutiveTickFaults`, `GameServer.FatalError`, Program.cs | ours | ours | none |
| Bans | `--ban-file`: one IP address or CIDR range per line (the address needs a dot or a colon: a bare number is ignored), `#` comments; checked every 2 s and read again when its time or size changes (a file written in the last 2 s is read once more); banned sources get no reply at all and connected banned players are dropped; a missing file bans no one | s | wall clock (server) | `ServerOptions.BanFile`, `BanList`, `BanFile` | ours | ours | none |
| Refusal detail | a content mismatch names the server's Steam build (from `appmanifest_55150.acf` two folders above the install, read-only, when present) and content fingerprint; the server logs every refusal with the client's protocol, content, config or map hash (throttled per address) | - | per refusal | `GameServer.ContentMismatchDetail`, `NoteRefusal` | ours | ours | none |
| UDP receive | read until the socket reports nothing (`Poll`, then `ReceiveFrom` until would-block), not while `Available` > 0 (on Linux 0 for an empty datagram, which then blocked every packet behind it); at most 256 empty, oversized or failed datagrams skipped per call; the server socket is bound with exclusive address use on Windows, and a port in use stops the server with exit code 3 | datagrams | per call | `DatagramReceive.Next`, `UdpServerTransport` | ours | ours | none |

Open (not done): a `BlobChunk` (an emblem upload chunk, protocol 22) carries no session; the server takes it only from a connection
with a player and only for an upload it asked that connection for, and checks the whole emblem's hash before use, but a sender that
can spoof that player's address could disturb its upload (worst case: the upload fails verification and is retried later).

Open (not done, S2 of the hardening review): lag compensation trusts the client's acknowledged snapshot within the 15-tick (500 ms) rewind
cap, so a client can fake up to 500 ms of lag; bounding the rewind by a server-measured round trip is planned (docs/changes-from-original.md).

| Behavior | Description | Kind | Confidence | Source / validation needed |

| Health recovery | Armour or shield regenerates over time. Health is restored mainly by executions and by Fury. | public | medium | Regen values now extracted (above); executions and Fury not yet |
| Fury | Meter filled by combat; activation gives a melee frenzy or slowed-time aiming. Also restores health. | public | medium | Same |

| Exterminatus | Online co-op wave mode (post-launch update) against Orks and Chaos; `cp_maps__*` / `cp_map_*` arenas and `ebp_sets__mp_coop_*` installed | public | medium | Wave and AI data |
| Classes | Tactical, Assault, Devastator (and Chaos counterparts) | public | medium | wargear and blueprint data |
| Progression | Unlocks by multiplayer level | public | low | Data files |

## Unknown, needs evidence

How the extracted speeds and acceleration values combine in the original controller, how the original combines the jump pack's values (M14 model is an interpretation), camera blending, pitch relaxing and collision (offsets and FOV are read since M20; whether FOV is vertical is not stated); whether aim assist applied to the PC mouse;
whether shots leave from the camera, the muzzle or the eye, and whether the original tests shots against the ragdoll bodies (used as hit volumes since M20) or other shapes, posed or at rest; how the extracted weapon values combine (upgrades, shield, Exterminatus); melee timing of weapons other than the knife, melee targeting and lunge; execution trigger rules and
invulnerability (the evade's property windows are hyper armour against stuns, not invulnerability, M21); which reaction state a
reaction type enters (the reaction graph's state machine transitions are not decoded; M28 maps kinds to clip sets by name); how the
player triggers the heavy classes' displace kick; the original PC binding of the heavy strike; root motion vs code-driven movement (the evade
follows its clips' extracted motion since M21; walking and the jump pack do not); how long code keeps the ready posture after a shot (blend times are read since M27; other animation blend times are not); network tick rates of the original.

### Stomp impacts, the power sword and the jump-pack thrust (fx/impact-pass; client only, not simulated, no protocol change)

The owner's requests of 2026-10-29: stomps with "ground breaking/shockwaves/etc. to give the stomps impact and weight" (no smoke or dust), a power sword that "should glow blue and flare
up when hitting an enemy", and jump-pack thrusters whose trail starts at the exhaust and is much shorter ("reference the video": the reference flights show bright blue-white glows at the
nozzles and flames of about 1 to 3 m). Content: `SmContent.MeleeEffects` (the melee wargear's blast-strike and deployed effects), `SmContent.NozzleExit`; client: `NetworkView.MeleeFx.cs`,
`StompFx.cs`, `PowerBlade.cs`, `NetworkView.JumpFx.cs`, `FxPlayer` (`TrailScale`, `BeamScale`, `TrailByDistance`), `WeaponRig` (`TryMeleeMarker`, `MeleeMeshInHand`, the exhaust form of
`TryWornMarker`). Tools: `smtool fx-dump <game-dir|auto> <name|word>... [--list] [--fields]`, `smtool fx-dump auto --map <map> [--where]`, `smtool weapon-parts <wargear> --markers
--profile <locator,locator> --exhaust <word>`.

### Ground pound impact and landing effects (M41; client only, not simulated, no protocol change)

From the owner's playtest (2026-10-28; user's knowledge of the original): a ground pound should leave a large impact on the ground with a small crater, a larger thin dark ring
where the pound's hit detection reached (natural, not bright), dust going up around the impact, the original sound, and perhaps physics chunks of the ground thrown about.

`GroundShards.cs`, `NetworkView.PoundImpact.cs`, `FxPlayer` (collisions, `PlaceTextureDecal`), `NetworkView.Sound.cs`. Test aid: `FxTest --pound-test` (see below).

### Test bots: aim error, engagement range, spawn-door wait, launcher and side requests (M44a; client and server option, test aids, not simulated, no protocol change)

From the owner's playtest (2026-10-28): bots should move better, wait outside an enemy spawn room instead of hugging its door, miss most of their shots (recorded footage), shoot
from across the map when they see the target, and be startable in numbers (up to 6 per side). **All of it is ours: test aids, not the original AI.** Human clients are untouched
(every rule below runs only under `--bot`; the server option is off by default). Code: `src/SmNet/BotAimModel.cs`, `client/NetworkView.BotAim.cs`, `NetworkView.BotSpawn.cs`,
`NetworkView.Bot.cs`, `NetworkView.Nav.cs`, `src/SmSim/NavAgent.cs`, `tools/bots.ps1` (`bots.cmd`), `MatchRules.HonorSideRequests` (`--honor-side-requests`).

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bot aim error | a bot that is shooting a ranged weapon at an enemy has its view (yaw, pitch) drifted off the line to the target by a slow **wander** (Ornstein-Uhlenbeck, time constant 1.5 s: a smooth move, no 30 Hz shake), and every tick the trigger is held its **shot** is turned by a fresh Gaussian **scatter through the protocol's shot offsets** (`PlayerInput.ShotYawOffset`/`ShotPitchOffset`, protocol 12; the body does not shake); per axis total σ = wander (0.8 σ) and scatter (0.6 σ) added in quadrature. Melee, grenade throws and every non-shooting tick keep the exact aim (the wander only drifts); the move stick is turned back so the body goes the same way. Seeded by player id (the same seed gives the same error sequence; a run as a whole does not repeat exactly) | radians | per input tick | `BotAimModel`, `NetworkView.BotApplyAim` | ours | test aid | none |
| `--bot-accuracy a` | the fraction of shots meant to hit at medium range (15 m) on a body of effective radius 0.5 m: σ = (0.5 / 15) / sqrt(-2 ln(1 - a)) per axis (a = 0.25: σ = 2.52°; a = 0.03: σ = 7.8°; a ≥ 0.999: no error). **Default 0.03** (lowered from 0.25 on the owner's request of 2026-10-28: "the bots when testing still absolutely obliterate me ... my thought is that they should have low accuracy"; with the trigger discipline below and the weapons' own scatter, weapons/spread) for a plain `--bot`; **1 (no error) when a probe or test-aid flag is present** that needs the shots to land (`--aim-test`, `--bot-stand`, `--hip-probe`, `--reload-capture`, `--reload-test`, `--look-closeup`, `--look-churn`, `--look-log`, `--camera-probe`, `--camera-selftest`, `--yaw-probe`, `--pan-rate`, `--bot-gait`, `--anim-probe`, `--motion-probe`, `--damage-demo`, `--picker-demo`, `--action-sweep`, `--gait-sweep`); an explicit `--bot-accuracy` wins. ### Connect timeout, hosting checks and hosted bots (fix/connect-timeout; client, front end and release launcher; no protocol change)

From the owner's report of the tester release (build 4fa4d46): an old server still held UDP 27015, the front end's hosted server could not bind it and exited (code 3), JOIN then
reached the old server, which dropped this version's Hello unread (servers from before 2026-10-28 had no refusal for another version's Hello), and the client showed
"Connecting" forever. Then the owner's requests of 2026-10-29: a STOP SERVER button, bots in a hosted match ("no bots are joining after successfully hosting", "add 7 bots on local
pc only server hosting initiation"), and + BOT / − BOT. fix/hosting-bots-logs (the owner's decisions of 2026-10-29, after a tester's 8 GB laptop ran out of memory
with the 7 default bots and the bots' logs pushed the player's own log out): no bots by default, one BOTS stepper (0 to 15) applied at the start, no + BOT / − BOT, and
every bot writes its own log file. **All values here are ours.** Code: `SmNet.ConnectFailure`, `GameClient` (`ClientStatus.NoAnswer`), `SmNet.MatchFlowGate`,
`SmContent.HostStart`, `SmContent.HostBots`, `client/FrontEnd/HostPanel.cs`, `HostedServer.cs`, `HostedBots.cs`, `tools/release/package/Host.cmd`, `Launcher.ps1 -StartBots`.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

### Performance pass 1 (perf/pass-1; build, client and release launcher; no protocol change)

The owner's report on the e792504 tester build hosted "This PC only" (the server, 7 headless bots and the owner's client on one PC). Measured on one PC
(a current desktop CPU and a current high-end GPU) by replaying one recorded 8-player Manufactorum demo (`--play-demo`, windowed off-screen, `--frame-profile`, the new
`--perf-probe`), the e792504 playtest zip against an export of this branch; other Godot runs shared the PC, so single runs vary by about 1.5 ms
(interleaved repeats). Before / after with 7 bots on the same PC: mean frame **12.0 → 6.4 ms**, p99 20.2 → 12.9 ms, p99.9 37.9 → 17.5 ms, frames over
33 ms 24 → 1 in 90 s; with no bots 7.5 → 5.3 ms, 4 → 0. Causes and fixes:
the exported game compiled SmSim, SmNet, SmContent and SmFormats without JIT optimisation (Godot's `ExportRelease` configuration is not one
Microsoft.NET.Sdk optimises; `Directory.Build.props` now does: collision rays 6 to 8.6 times faster, the follow camera 1.8 → 0.2 ms a frame);
`HitVolumes.Bounds` took a hull's margin again for every corner (20 to 45 ms on the crosshair ray while a jump-pack player flew, Debug; same result now);
the first ammunition drop's model was read on the main thread (100 to 140 ms, about 20 s into every match; now during the map load); a blocking full
collection of the .NET GC (88 ms once). Code: `client/BotLean.cs`, `client/PerfProbe.cs`, `NetworkView.Pickups.cs` (`PrewarmPickups`), `SmNet.LeanBot`.
Merged with perf/lean-bots (integrate/2026-10-29): perf/pass-1's `--bot-lean` flag is gone; its frame cap, physics rate and `--no-fx` apply to every lean bot
(`LeanBot.Decide`: a headless `--bot` without `--bot-full-load` or a presentation aid), whose skipped loads (map visuals included) are perf/lean-bots'.

| Parameter | Value | Units | Timing basis | Where | Source | Kind | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lean bot frame cap | a lean bot (`LeanBot.Decide`: the hosted match's bots, `bots.cmd`, `Launcher.ps1 -StartBots`) runs at most **30** frames a second (`--bot-fps n` overrides, 0 = no cap; Godot's own `--max-fps` before `--` wins); before, a headless bot ran uncapped at about 134 | frames/s | per frame | `LeanBot.FrameCap`, `LeanBot.FrameCapFor`, `BotLean.Apply` | ours (the server's 30 Hz tick: one input a tick) | ours | none |
| Lean bot physics steps | **30** a second (a lean bot builds no ragdolls or physics props; Godot's default 60) | steps/s | engine physics | `LeanBot.PhysicsTicks` | ours | ours | none |
| Lean bot content | no effects (`--no-fx`); everything else perf/lean-bots skips (row "Lean headless bot": the map's visuals, sound, looks, weapons, ragdolls, poses, ...); collision, navigation, characters and everything the bot decides from are loaded | — | per bot | `BotLean`, `NetworkView.Lean.cs` | ours | ours | none |
| Human client GC mode | `GCLatencyMode.SustainedLowLatency` for a client that is not a bot (no blocking full collection unless memory runs low); `--gc-default` keeps the runtime's default | — | per process | `ModelViewer.StartNetwork` | ours | ours | none |
| Probe (`--perf-probe`) | every 5 s and at the end: frame times, the renderer's CPU and GPU time, draw calls, objects, primitives, physics step, video memory, node, light (with shadows), decal, particle and mesh counts, managed heap, bytes allocated per frame, collections, working set | ms, counts, MB | per 5 s | `client/PerfProbe.cs` | test aid | - | - |

Since O5 the Ork plays: `smserver` and the networked client both load `GameplayTuning.LoadForMatch` (the Ork Boy as class 6 in Parity; `--ork-data` on both
for the data's values), so their config hashes agree (the install's: `28070D2ECC8C9C09` with the Ork in Parity; a marine or Chaos class hashes as before,
a class's race is hashed only when it has one). The Hello and the Setup carry the Ork look; the `Appearance` message carries race 3. Snapshots, scoreboard,
kill feed and shot records are unchanged (worst case 1200 bytes). Code: `SmSim/Appearance.cs` (`Race`, `Races`, `OrkAppearanceRules`), `SmNet/Protocol.cs`,
`SmServer/GameServer.cs`, `SmServer/GameServer.Appearance.cs`, `SmNet/GameClient*.cs`; tests `OrkWireTests`, `OrkBalanceTests.TheMatchConfigHashesAlike…`.
Not done here: the networked Ork model and animation (O7: a joining Ork is drawn as the default marine placeholder until then), the customizer's faction
step and look row (O9: the client sends the look "automatic" until then).

### The networked Ork: model and locomotion (Ork O7a; client only, not simulated, no protocol change)

A player whose class has the Ork race (`Races.Of(config, class, team) == Race.Orks`) is drawn as an Ork: the boy's original skinned meshes on the boy's own rig
(`OrkAssets`, a rig of 51 bones, so a character is replaced, not re-skinned, when its player changes race), its weapons on the boy's prop bones (`WeaponRig`, O6) and
its movement from the boy's own clips. Code: `client/NetworkView.Ork.cs` (hooks in `NetworkView.cs` `Place` / `Spawn`, `NetworkView.Appearance.cs` `EnsureModel`,
`NetworkView.Weapons.cs`, `NetworkView.Death.cs`, `NetworkView.Prewarm.cs`, `CharacterViewer.LegIk.cs`, `WeaponAssets.FromCatalogue`), engine-free rules in
`SmContent/OrkLocomotion.cs` (`OrkLookRules`, `OrkLocomotionPlan`, `OrkPitchClip`; tests `OrkLocomotionTests`). `smtool graph-dump --gaits --rig ork` prints the plan and the
measured gaits, `--bones --rig ork` the skeleton. `--no-ork-model` (test aid) draws Orks as the default marine, as before O7a. **Not done here** (done in O7b / O7c, next section):
hit reactions, the charge clip, melee swings, the dodge hop, the death clips, the shot recoil, the reload clip, the throw's release mapping; still absent: the body-turn / run-start
/ foot-pin rules of the marines (the boy's graphs have none), Ork sounds (O8).

### The networked Ork: actions and reactions (Ork O7b / O7c; client only, not simulated, no protocol change)

The boy's own clips for what an Ork does and what happens to it, laid over the times the simulation already runs (the marine's timings for reactions and the throw, the Ork's own
from O4 for the choppa, the charge and the hop). Code: `client/NetworkView.OrkActions.cs` (`OrkActionPose`, in the marines' order: reaction, charge, melee, hop, throw, then
locomotion with the recoil and the reload over it; hooks in `NetworkView.cs` `Place` / `SetUpClasses`, `NetworkView.ClipSmoothing.cs`, `NetworkView.Reload.cs`,
`NetworkView.Reactions.cs`, `NetworkView.Death.cs`, `NetworkView.Weapons.cs`); engine-free reader and rules in `SmContent/OrkActions.cs` (`OrkActions`, `OrkActionPlan`,
`OrkActionRules`; tests `OrkActionsTests`), read with the locomotion on one worker (`OrkLocomotionBundle.Actions`; the action clips are decoded there too). `smtool ork-actions
<game-dir|auto>` prints every clip, its timing and the rate it plays at. Test aids: `--no-ork-actions` (the O7a movement pose only), `--ork-capture <dir>` (windowed client:
screenshots of each action half way, inside the private data folder). The marine and Chaos paths are unchanged (`Place` hands a character on the Ork rig to `PlaceOrk` first; the
marine hooks only skip the Ork class's clips, which are not marine-rig clips). Labels: *original asset loaded* for every clip; the stretching of a clip to the simulation's time is
**ours** (design section 5: "stretched to the sim's marine timings"; parity: the Ork keeps the Tactical's reaction, throw and hop timings), the choices of clip where the boy has no
exact one are **interpretation**.

### Ork sounds and barks (Ork O8; client only, not simulated, no protocol change)

What the data binds for the Ork Boy and what the client plays for it. Read with `smtool ork-sounds <game-dir|auto>` (each sound and speech command of the boy's blueprint
`ork_coop_boy` and the Ork wargear resolved against the banks: voices per post, the speech bank's line for his voice; then the behaviour tags of the boy rig's clips and what binds
them). Code: `SmContent/OrkSounds.cs` (names, rules, tested in `OrkSoundTests`), `SoundTriggers` (the Ork blueprint joins `PlayerBlueprints`; the boy rig's clip tags join the marine
rig's table; the Ork class's speech character is the blueprint's), `client/NetworkView.Sound.Ork.cs`, hooks in `NetworkView.Sound.cs` (`BlueprintName`, `SoundOrk`), `NetworkView.Match.cs`
(`OrkKillSound`) and `SoundSystem.StopSpeech`. A player of the Ork race sounds as an Ork whether or not the Ork model is drawn; before O8 it played the marine blueprint's spawn and death
sounds and nothing else. `--log-sound ork` prints every Ork post with the voices it resolved to; `--no-ork-silly` switches off the roar and taunt (ours).

### Added content: the content switch (E1; server, client and config hash; no protocol change)

faction, mode or mechanic SM1 multiplayer did not have (the Ork Boy, gore), removable in one piece; the owner's changes to things SM1 had (bolter

### Added content: Musou — the Three-Front War: the war between the battles (TF2: `WarSim`, not yet driven by a match)

### Death effects (F-D1; client only, not simulated, no protocol change)

The effects the original multiplayer data itself binds to a marine's or Chaos marine's death (faithful content, not the gore extras of `docs/gore-design.md`). Read at run time from the install by `SmContent/DeathEffects.cs`
(`DeathEffects`, `DeathAction`, `DeathEffectRules`; tested in `DeathEffectsTests`), played by `client/NetworkView.DeathFx.cs` when the ragdoll starts. Evidence, with the `smtool baf-dump` calls that found it: `docs/discovery.md` "Death effects (F-D1)".
Nothing is severed or removed: the marine armour has no stump or wound geometry, and the effects are particles at bones. Open question for the owner: did a plasma or melta kill visibly remove a limb or the body in multiplayer? (The data names the effects "limb vanish" and "vaporize limb", and a `remove_wargear` step makes the corpse's ranged weapon disappear 1.2 s after a plasma death; no mesh element is in any of them.)

### Flying hitboxes, the view fraction, the grenade bounce and the bots' damage scale (fix/hitboxes-grenades-bots; protocol 37)

From the owner's playtest (2026-10-29, verbatim): "it feels difficult to shoot enemy assault marines or raptors while they're flying. check on their hitboxes. also they're
absolutely murdering me quickly with their bolt pistols. reduce all bot damage by 66% temporarily for testing purposes." and "grenades shouldn't bounce so far when thrown."
Code: `src/SmSim/FlightHitVolumes.cs` (`FlightVolumes`, `SimConfig.HitBody`), `src/SmContent/PosedHitVolumes.cs`, `src/SmContent/FlightHitVolumes.cs`, `src/SmSim/RewindFraction.cs`
(`World.SeenAt`, `World.Between`), `GameClient.ViewOf`, `RigidSpec.Bounce` / `GroundMaterial`, `OwnerBalance.WithGrenadeBounce`, `src/SmSim/DamageScale.cs`, `--bot-damage-scale`.
Probes: `smtool hitbox-probe <game-dir|auto>`, `FlyingHitboxProbe` and `GrenadeBounceProbe` (install tests, skipped without the install); synthetic tests `FlyingHitboxTests`.

### Player collision (sim/player-collision; protocol 43, used by the simulation)

From the owner's request (2026-10-29, verbatim): "improve player model collision. the models shouldn't get stuck inside each other." Before this branch players did not
collide with each other at all in the simulation: every player's movement step saw only the level, the props and the other side's spawn-room blockers, so two players
walked, charged, were knocked and landed straight through each other; only the cameras were pushed out of bodies (M40-T6) and the charge's contact test measured
distances. The original's Havok character proxies block each other (players cannot stand inside each other in SM1), but how its controller resolves them is not decoded:
every rule below is ours. Code: `src/SmSim/PlayerCollision.cs` (`PlayerCollision`, `BodyView`, `PlayerBody`), `src/SmSim/WorldBodies.cs` (`World.RecordBodies`,
`BodiesFor`, `LeastCrowded`), `Movement.Step` / `Glide` / `Fly`, `src/SmNet/GameClient.Bodies.cs`, `GameServer.WithBoundedBody`, `src/SmNet/DrawnBodies.cs`,
`client/NetworkView.Bodies.cs`, `src/SmSim/OverlapProbe.cs`. Tests: `PlayerCollisionTests`. Test aids: server `--no-player-collision` (with the same switch on every client:
config hash) and `--log-overlaps`; client `--no-player-collision`, `--no-body-separation`; a bot logs drawn overlaps and prediction corrections every 10 s.

| Parameter (sim/player-collision) | Value | Units | Timing basis | Where | Source | Kind | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Who collides | every living player with every other living player, allies and enemies alike, in every way of moving (walk, sprint, sprint stop, evades, knockback, the charge and the dash attack, melee lunges and the lock's root motion, jump-pack flight, the pound and slash dives, falls); the dead (ragdolls), pickups and projectiles do not; `SimConfig.PlayerBodies` (on; off only with the test switch, hashed only when off) | — | per tick | `Movement.Step` / `Glide` / `Fly`, `PlayerCollision` | the owner's request; the scope ours | ours | medium |

| What a step collides with (prediction-exact) | the others as the stepping player's client last knew them: each input names the newest snapshot its client held when it was sampled (`PlayerInput.BodyTick`, one byte on the wire: ticks back from the input, 1 to 24; 0 = none); the server keeps every tick's end state for 64 ticks (`World.RecordBodies`, the same floats the snapshot after it carries) and both sides take that tick's living players. The client's prediction, its replays and the server therefore step with the same bodies (measured with a temporary trace over 16,300 ticks of an 8-bot run: no tick where client and server stepped the same input from the same state with different bodies); a step depends only on past ticks, so the server's player order changes nothing | ticks | per input | `World.BodiesFor`, `GameClient.BodyTickFor` / `BodiesFor`, `PlayerCollision.See` | ours (standard client prediction; the original was peer-hosted) | ours | medium |

Without the carry two sprinters meet a round trip too late and run through each other; without the stop a runner who stopped against the player is carried on past it | ticks, m | per input | `PlayerCollision.See`, `Where`, `MaxExtrapolationTicks`, `MaxExtrapolation` | ours | ours | low |
| Blocking and sliding | the part of a move going into a body the player touches or overlaps is removed; the rest sweeps the two capsules' circles (0.9 m) and slides along the first one met (up to 4 slides a tick, no tunnelling at any speed); the velocity loses what went into the body, as against a wall (a blocked charge or lunge stops at contact range, 0.9 m between axes) | m | per tick | `PlayerCollision.Resolve` | ours | ours | medium |
| Push apart | two capsules that overlapped sideways in the snapshot are pushed apart along the line between their axes there (a tie on one spot: one of 8 fixed directions from the two ids, opposite for each): each player moves out **half** the overlap (the other half is the other's own step), less what it has already moved out along that line since the snapshot, at most **3 m/s**; the push is not velocity. Measuring from the snapshot keeps a crowd from rocking (pushing on the stale picture of now overshot by a round trip's worth). Two players on one spot are 0.9 m apart after 5 ticks | m/s | per tick | `PlayerCollision.Push`, `SeparationSpeed` | ours | ours | low |
| On a head | feet within 0.3 m below another capsule's top and at most 0.05 m above it are on its head: not blocked sideways, they slide off at **6 m/s** (the whole overlap); a body coming down onto a head (a fall, a jump-pack landing) is held at the head's top, not grounded and not falling, until it has slid off (2 to 5 ticks); a ground pound's or slash's dive lands on the head in the tick it touches it (review fix: its impact then, at the head's height, not 0.1 to 0.3 s later beside the victim), then slides off in its recovery; bodies above a player's head band are the upper player's to resolve | m, m/s | per tick | `PlayerCollision.Relate`, `Finish`, `OnTopBand`, `HeadReach`, `SlideOffSpeed` | ours | ours | low |

| Charge against a target that brakes (playtest item) | the charge is stopped 0.9 m from the target as the charger's client carried it on (its velocity at the snapshot); a target that braked or turned since is really farther, so the charge can stop short and its contact (2 x 0.45 + 0.3 m, on the rewound target) whiff where it hit before player collision. To check in a playtest: charges at targets that stop or dodge late | m | per charge | `PlayerCollision.See`, `Rush.Contact` | ours | ours | low |
| Evades | a roll, hop or dash met by a body within the wall-hit angle ends as at a wall; the push apart is left out of that test (review fix: being pushed by a stale overlap is not being stopped, so a roll started while overlapping does not end at once) | ° | per tick | `Evade.Step`, `PlayerCollision.LastPush` | ours | ours | low |

| Server bound (review fix) | the world itself never collides with a picture older than **24 ticks** (0.8 s: the shot rewind's 15 ticks plus the view slack): an older body tick is raised to 24 ticks back, and on the server (`World.BoundBodies`) so is none (lag byte 0, or a lag beyond 24, which the wire drops to 0), whatever the client acknowledges, so a client cannot shed the bodies and walk through players; tools and tests without the bound keep 0 = no bodies. On top, a body tick older than the snapshot the input's batch acknowledged, less the view slack (the longest interpolation delay + 4 ticks), is raised to that bound. An honest client names its newest snapshot and predicts exactly; one whose newest snapshot is more than 24 ticks old (over about 450 ms RTT, or a stall) or a join's first ticks before its first snapshot predict without bodies while the server has them. A repeated input (lost packets) keeps its body tick relative to its own tick | ticks | per input | `World.BodiesFor`, `World.BoundBodies`, `PlayerCollision.MaxBodyLagTicks`, `GameServer.WithBoundedBody`, `BodySlack` | ours | ours | medium |

(the charge key, the holstered reloads, the melee direction), `Rush.WHeld`, `Rush.DashOffset`, `PlayerState.OtherReloadLeft` / `ThirdReloadLeft` / `MeleeDirection`, `FallRules.ChargeShowsFall`

### The feel pass: the roll's blending for every action (anim/feel-pass; client only, not simulated, no protocol change)

Sources: the owner's playtest notes of 2026-10-30, item 15 and its interview ("the tactical roll is PERFECT ... make the rest of the animations/actions blend and transition that well and in the
same style"; most wrong: movement weight, melee impact, transitions; worst: move ↔ shoot / aim, into / out of melee, combo chains, the air slash's landing). The base graph's transitions were
read with `smtool graph-dump SM_Base_MP --no-tree` and `MP_SM_NAV_JP_Sim`. Code: `client/NetworkView.Feel.cs` (the pattern in its class comment), `NetworkView.SprintEdges.cs` (`ExitBlendOf`),
`NetworkView.Jump.cs`, `CharacterViewer.cs` (the layer fold, the clip restart), `SmNet.SlashPose.SmoothDiveTime` (test `SlashPoseTests`). Measured with `--transition-probe --transition-probe-clips`
and `--anim-probe` on one recorded session (`feel/sweep1`, 165 s, protocol 45: a Tactical with `--transition-sweep` recording, an Assault with `--slash-test`, a Raptor and a Devastator with
`--transition-sweep`, a Chaos Tactical with `--bot-melee`), replayed headless at 60 fps, `--no-feel` for the before. Test aids: `--no-feel` (every change of this section off), the probe's new
`bob` lines (the pelvis's height and sideways range over 48-frame windows of one state, by speed band), its aim / ready labels, and a replay's connect timeout of 10 minutes (a demo recorded beside
other loading clients waited more than the live 10 s for its Welcome and replayed as "no answer").

### Sticky launcher grenades (sim/sticky-launcher; protocol 48, used by the simulation)

Source: the owner (2026-10-31): "vengeance launcher grenades should not bounce. they should instantly stick to whatever they strike. they can also stick to players." The data agrees in part: `grenade_launcher_grenade_multiplayer` has `sticky` true and `detonate_on_collision` false (row "Projectile `grenade_launcher_grenade_multiplayer`"); its `max_bounce_count` 1 is what made the old rule bounce once off the level before sticking. will trigger/work."; C "when falling as assault marine/raptor, if i am falling out of a ledge or out of a jump, i am not able to short hop (space bar tap). i should be able to perform a

evade, jump-pack and buffer tests). Measured with a scratch probe on the install's config (buildid 7412325, not committed).

A melee or heavy press in the dash's start tick refuses the dash, here and on the ground alike, so the press acts (the review's L2).
